items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: The interviewer lists John Simmons as a member of the Basie band ('We got John Simmons on bass') in the context of introducing a recording, but the interviewee (Jo Jones) does not speak about his personal relationship with Simmons in the provided text.

ctx.x: of the very great work of some of the great Basie men like you and Buck Clayton, and here's Lester Young on tenor and clarinet, showing what a great clarinet player he was which people have forgotten sometimes I think. We also will hear some of the great work of Joe, (Walter Page), of Walter Page, and Eddie Durham - a great, great name in jazz, whose electric guitar and trombone are still around with us in 1973. I'd like to play this. The other side of this has got "Three Little Words", "Four O'Clock Drag", and…

items.title: 56800_John Simmons oral history interview
items.q: the first time that I saw him... I couldn't stand him... I didn't know that until I went to New York and I found this out.

ctx.x: Did you work with him in New York?
No. We palmed around a lot. And he was the -- (laughter) -- you know Jo Jones had a language all his own (unintelligible), never know what he was talking about. Now
Lester would never swear. If he wanted to say M. F., he would say "Orrin Tucker" and if he wanted to say K. M. A., he'd say "Whispering Grass" (Laughter).
